messages.task:
You are a financial-analytics assistant.  Your task is to answer questions about Citi’s Brokerage and Asset Management (BAM) segment using the tools you have been given.

Scenario context (extracted from the annual report narrative):
Citi’s Brokerage and Asset Management segment (BAM) represented about 6 % of Citi Holdings by assets as of December 31 2009.  The segment was materially reshaped during 2009 after divestitures such as Smith Barney (to the Morgan Stanley Smith Barney joint venture – MSSB JV) and Nikko Cordial Securities.  At year-end 2009 BAM reported approximately $35 billion of assets, including a 49 % stake in MSSB JV (booked as $13 billion investments and $13 billion client-related loans) and around $9 billion of other asset-management and insurance businesses.  Morgan Stanley has options to purchase Citi’s remaining MSSB JV stake starting in 2012.  During 2009 Citi recorded an $11.1 billion pretax gain ($6.7 billion after tax) on the Smith Barney sale.  Management commentary highlights that revenue movements were heavily influenced by these portfolio changes and the absence of several divested businesses in the comparison periods.

Available tools (use them whenever you need information):
• list_business_units() ➜ list of all business-unit names in the database.
• fetch_business_unit_id(name) ➜ internal numeric id for a business unit.
• list_metric_names() ➜ list of every metric captured in the data warehouse.
• fetch_metric_id(metric_name) ➜ internal numeric id for a metric.
• fetch_metric_value_by_ids(business_unit_id, year, metric_id) ➜ numeric metric value (in millions) for the requested unit, year and metric.
• calculate_percentage(numerator, denominator) ➜ return "XX%" rounded to the nearest whole percent.
• get_random_metric_value(year) ➜ returns a random metric value (mostly irrelevant, included for completeness).
• get_average_metric_across_units(metric_name, year) ➜ average value of a metric across all business units (also not essential for most targeted questions).

Question you must answer:
As a percent of total revenues net of interest expense, what was non-interest revenue in 2009?

Think through which tools give you the data you need, call them as necessary, and provide the final answer as an exact percentage such as “97%”.
